summary: Assess pivoting the paper to a planner-agnostic certified semantic-risk safety layer (MINCO as carrier or side product)
logs: 4 lanes: epsilon math x2, literature x2, code carryover, data feasibility
investigation lanes done; convening 3-lens judge panel

analyses.verdict: A workable epsilon budget exists, but only at the per-encounter, per-agent-trajectory level — never per-(agent,timestep). With eps=0.1 split as eps_cls=0.02 / eps_pred=0.08, a time-shaped max-over-horizon score per agent (Lindemann RA-L 2023 style) and a union bound over at most H=10 agents gives alpha=0.008, n_min=124 calibration trajectories per Mondrian cell (~1,250 for stable quantiles), terminal tube radius ~0.9 m with a learned predictor (~2.0 m with constant-velocity) — operationally meaningful in a few-meter corridor, but only barely, and only if the constant-velocity predictor debt is paid. The naive per-(agent,timestep) union bound is dead on arrival: alpha=1.3e-4 at (H=10,T=30,eps_pred=0.04) sits at the 99.99th percentile of a heavy-tailed error distribution, giving ~4.6-4.8 m tube radii (4x the 95% radius) that block any corridor, and 7,499 minimum / ~75,000 comfortable calibration trajectories PER Mondrian cell. The paper survives if the headline guarantee is restated as per-encounter (whole 2-3 s horizon, single planning episode) and the per-mission claim is dropped or handled with an explicit replan-cycle union; it dies if reviewers are promised per-timestep guarantees in crowds at eps=0.05.
key_points: Sensible split: eps_cls = 0.2*eps, eps_pred = 0.8*eps (classification miss is unrecoverable because hard constraints never engage; tube exit is still catchable by the RTA monitor) -> (0.01,0.04) at eps=0.05, (0.02,0.08) at eps=0.1; execution covered deterministically by post-hoc verification + fallback, budget ~0.

Naive design is fatal not mainly via n (7,499 unstratified is borderline vs a 10^4 dataset) but via tube width: at alpha~1e-4 the conformal quantile is the calibration-set maximum of a heavy-tailed distribution -> ~4x the 95% radius (~4.6-4.8 m vs 1.2 m at 3 s for CV prediction), one tube spans the entire corridor, and the quantile has max-statistic variance (one ID-switch glitch in calibration inflates every tube).
Naive x Mondrian is arithmetically impossible: 7,499 min (75k comfortable) per cell x 9-18 cells = 67k-1.35M trajectories vs ~10^4 available.

Minimum viable design = (d)~(a)+(b): per-agent functional score s_i = max_t ||e_t||/rho(t) with a time-shaping function rho(t) (so the tube grows with horizon instead of carrying terminal error back to t=0), union bound only over agents: alpha = eps_pred/H; exchangeability unit = one agent-trajectory per encounter, which is exactly what SDD provides.

Escape (c) max-over-agents-per-scene is a trap: it makes the score distribution depend on H, manufacturing the very density-shift coverage collapse that contribution (1) then fixes — Pappas-lineage reviewers will call this circular; with per-agent scores the H-dependence is an explicit, honest union bound and much of the 'collapse' phenomenon disappears. Reframe contribution (1) as fixing residual class/density shift of per-agent error distributions, not as rescuing scene-level scores.

Escape (e): Cleaveland-style time-parameterized quantile optimization buys back maybe 2-3x volume vs the uniform union but costs a data split (fit alpha_t on D1, calibrate on D2) — affordable only in the 2-3 cell sparse bins; CopulaCPTS's finite-sample guarantee is approximate (copula estimation error), so it cannot carry a 'mathematical upper bound' headline — use both as comparison baselines, not as the certificate core.

Hidden multiplicities the eps-arithmetic must confess: (i) 10 Hz replanning = a fresh conformal claim per cycle, so per-mission P(hit) needs another union over ~600 cycles/min unless restated per-encounter; (ii) eps_cls is per-detection-per-frame — a persistent track over 30 frames needs a one-shot-per-track decision rule or it silently re-introduces a T-factor on the classification side; (iii) collision != tube exit: tubes must additionally be inflated by drone body radius + tracking error (deterministic, ~0.5 m) before the corridor-width math is honest.

Calibration data reality: SDD is ~10^4 agent-trajectories but heavily class-imbalanced (cart/skateboarder are percent-level), so 6 classes x 3 density bins starves rare crowded cells; collapse to {human, vehicle-like, other} x {sparse, crowded} = 6 cells. Also SDD->Isaac-Sim is itself a distribution shift that violates exchangeability; ACI patches it but only gives asymptotic average coverage, which contradicts the finite-sample headline — say so explicitly or calibrate in-sim.

Claims to weaken: per-timestep -> per-encounter guarantee; per-mission -> per-planning-episode; 'arbitrary correlation' theorem is a one-line union bound (valid, but novelty must come from the system, not the theorem); 'bound still holds sparse->crowded' holds only within calibrated density bins up to H_max=10, not for arbitrary crowds.
numbers: Tube radius at 3 s, learned predictor (median 0.25 m, q95=0.60 m): r(0.05)=0.60 m, r(0.0267)=0.70 m, r(0.008)=0.90 m, r(1.33e-4)=1.74 m.
Corridor blockage: blocked band = 2*(r + 0.5 m drone+tracking); r=2.0 m -> 5.0 m > 4 m corridor (one pedestrian blocks it); r=0.9 m -> 2.8 m (passable).

Escape (c): alpha = eps_pred -> n_min = 24 (0.04) or 12 (0.08) scenes per cell, but score = max over H agents, so radius re-inflates roughly like the per-agent quantile at alpha/H anyway — no free lunch, just hidden.

Mondrian totals (per-agent design, density bins H_max={1,3,10}): eps_pred=0.08 -> per-class n_min=173, 3 classes=519, 6 classes=1,038; comfortable 10x = 5,250 / 10,500. eps_pred=0.04 -> per-class 347; 3cls=1,041, 6cls=2,082; 10x = 10,500 / 21,000 (at/over the 10^4 dataset).
Naive x Mondrian: 7,499 x 9 = 67,491 minimum; 75,000 x 18 = 1.35M comfortable — infeasible.
Non-vacuity condition: rank ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)) <= n  <=>  n >= (1-alpha)/alpha = 1/alpha - 1; at n = n_min the quantile equals the sample maximum.
risks: Reviewer-circularity risk on contribution (1): density-shift coverage collapse is largely an artifact of scene-level scoring; with per-agent scores plus explicit H union bound the phenomenon shrinks, weakening the headline diagnosis.
ACI delivers long-run average coverage, not finite-sample per-flight bounds — using it anywhere in the chain quietly downgrades the headline 'mathematical upper bound' to an asymptotic statement.

Heavy-tail sensitivity: all radius numbers assume lognormal tails; real pedestrian errors (stops, reversals) can be worse, and at n near n_min the quantile = calibration max, so a single outlier trajectory inflates every deployed tube.

Hidden unions not in the current budget: replan cycles (10 Hz x mission), per-frame classification on persistent tracks, detection/association failures (missed pedestrian = no tube at all — conformal classification cannot cover a detector miss).
SDD-calibrate / Isaac-deploy exchangeability violation; same-video trajectory correlation reduces effective n below nominal counts.

Constant-velocity prediction is the binding constraint: with CV, even the best design gives ~2 m tubes that make crowded scenes (H=10) largely infeasible — the planner will hover/yield constantly, which reviewers will read as the certificate being vacuous in exactly the crowded regime the paper advertises.
analyses.detail:
SETUP. Chain: P(hit) <= eps_cls + eps_pred with execution handled deterministically (post-hoc verification + RTA fallback => no stochastic budget). Split rationale: a missed 'human' label disables the hard-constraint path entirely (unrecoverable), but it is a single low-dimensional event per track, cheap to certify tightly; prediction tubes are where geometry costs live. Propose eps_cls = 0.2 eps, eps_pred = 0.8 eps: (0.01, 0.04) at eps=0.05 and (0.02, 0.08) at eps=0.1. Conformal classification at alpha_cls=0.01 needs only n >= 99 labeled detections per class cell — never the bottleneck; the per-frame-vs-per-track union is (see risks).

1-2. NAIVE per-(agent,timestep): alpha = eps_pred/(H T). Full table in numbers. Two formulas: alpha = eps_pred/(HT); n_min = ceil(1/alpha - 1) from rank ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)) <= n. Worst case (eps=0.05, H=10, T=30): alpha = 1.33e-4, n_min = 7,499. Usefulness: model 3 s CV prediction error as lognormal with median 0.40 m, q95 = 1.20 m => sigma = ln(3)/1.645 = 0.668; q_p = 0.40 exp(0.668 z_p). Then r(1.33e-4) = 4.57 m, r(1e-4) = 4.80 m — exactly the claimed 'several times the 95th percentile' (ratio 4.0x). Blocked band per pedestrian = 2(r + r_drone + e_track) ~ 2(4.6+0.5) = 10.2 m. In a 4 m corridor with 10 pedestrians this is not conservative planning, it is a certificate of permanent infeasibility. Additionally at n ~ n_min the quantile IS the calibration maximum (max-statistic variance). Verdict on naive: dead — primarily from tube width and Mondrian multiplication, not raw n.

3. ESCAPES. (a) Max-over-horizon score per agent prediction, R_i = max_t ||xhat_t - x_t|| (Lindemann et al. RA-L 2023): kills T; alpha = eps_pred/H. Exchangeability unit = agent-trajectory; calibration = n predicted-vs-realized pedestrian trajectories. Unnormalized version carries terminal error back to t=0 (2-3x inflation early in horizon). (b) is the same alpha arithmetic — numbers: eps_pred=0.08 gives alpha = 0.08/0.0267/0.008 and n_min = 12/37/124 for H = 1/3/10. Tube radius at H=10: 2.00 m (CV) or 0.90 m (learned). (c) Max-over-agents per scene: alpha = eps_pred, n_min = 12-24 scenes — cheapest, but score distribution now depends on H: this is precisely the density coupling of contribution (1). Synergy: Mondrian-by-density restores within-bin exchangeability. Circularity: the collapse being fixed was induced by the scoring choice; and the max-over-H quantile re-inflates to roughly the per-agent alpha/H level anyway (extreme-value arithmetic), so nothing is gained geometrically. (d) Whole-trajectory functional score s_i = max_t ||e_t||/rho(t) with shaping rho(t) (e.g., fitted sigma_t): same alpha/n as (a/b), but tube radius r(t) = q rho(t) grows with horizon — recovers per-step-like geometry without the T union. This is the minimum viable design. (e) Cleaveland et al. time-parameterized quantile optimization: allocates alpha_t with sum alpha_t <= alpha via LP on a held-out split; tighter than uniform union (order 2-3x volume) but needs D1+D2 split — only affordable in sparse cells; unit = trajectory. CopulaCPTS: estimates the inter-step copula; data-hungry and finite-sample validity only approximate — disqualified as the certificate core for an 'upper bound' headline, fine as baseline.

4. MONDRIAN. Cells = classes x density. Surviving design (d): alpha_cell = eps_pred/H_bin, H_bin in {1,3,10}. Per-class n_min = 173 (eps_pred=0.08) or 347 (0.04); totals: 3 classes = 519/1,041 minimum; 6 classes = 1,038/2,082; comfortable (10/alpha) = 5,250-21,000. Against ~10^4 agent-trajectories: 3 classes x 3 bins at eps=0.1 fits with margin; 6 classes or eps=0.05 at 10x comfort hits the dataset ceiling, and class imbalance (SDD rare classes at percent level) starves rare-x-crowded cells regardless of totals. Naive x Mondrian: 67k-1.35M — impossible.

5. VERDICT. Feasible budget: eps = 0.1, eps_cls = 0.02, eps_pred = 0.08, design (d), H capped at 10, <= 9 cells ({human, vehicle-like, other} x 3 density bins), learned predictor => 0.9 m terminal tubes, ~1,250 trajectories per crowded cell. eps = 0.05 is feasible only at H <= 3 or with merged density bins. Weaken: per-(agent,timestep) -> per-encounter ('P(realized trajectory exits its tube anywhere in the 3 s horizon)'); per-mission -> per-planning-episode (or add explicit replan union); 'arbitrary correlation' -> stated as union bound; 'sparse-to-crowded' -> 'within calibrated density bins up to H_max'. The single highest-leverage engineering item the arithmetic exposes: replace constant-velocity prediction before calibrating — the entire margin between 'meaningful 0.9 m tubes' and 'vacuous 2 m+ tubes' lives in the predictor's q95, not in the conformal machinery.

analyses.verdict: The theorem as headlined — "P(collision with a human) <= eps_cls + eps_pred, covering the whole chain, robust sparse-to-crowded" — is NOT provable as stated, for three structural reasons: (i) missed detections are outside every conformal certificate in the chain (Timans-style guarantees condition on a matched detection existing) and the FN rate RISES with the very density shift the paper headlines; (ii) data-association/tracking error is a real, unbudgeted third term whose omission breaks the exchangeability premise of the prediction tubes; (iii) substituting ACI for density shift silently converts a per-episode collision-probability bound into a long-run time-average miscoverage frequency, which is a different mathematical object (collisions are hitting events, and ACI permits miscoverage to concentrate exactly in the dense moments). The honest, provable version: a per-detected-track, per-episode bound eps_fn + eps_assoc + eps_cls + eps_pred under explicit named assumptions (within-stratum exchangeability for class-x-density Mondrian bins, pedestrian speed cap, non-reactive pedestrians, measured tracking-error inflation), with undetected humans handled by a DETERMINISTIC branch (unobserved/occluded space treated as adversarially occupied with speed cap — no statistical budget), association absorbed by calibrating tubes on tracker OUTPUT histories end-to-end, a latched per-track trigger so the per-frame classification bound legitimately becomes per-track, and ACI demoted to an empirical adaptation layer labeled as time-average. That version survives the Lindemann/Kantaros/Dixit reviewer pool and is arguably MORE novel (that lineage assumes perfect perception; a sound statistical+geometric hybrid covering FN/occlusion would be a real contribution). Given 3 months zero buffer: cut the second-planner demo before weakening the theorem.
key_points: Q1: marginal coverage DOES imply the joint bound P(Y=human AND human not in C(X)) <= eps_cls (the event is a subset of miscoverage), but it is semantically misleading — the per-human conditional miss rate can reach eps/pi_human (50% at eps=0.05, 10% human prior) — and it breaks under the label-prior shift that sparse-to-crowded causes.

Q1 fix: the correct statement is Mondrian-by-class — calibrate the threshold on human-only nonconformity scores to get P(human in C(X) | Y=human) >= 1−eps_cls, valid under within-class exchangeability and immune to label shift; requires n_h labeled human detections per stratum from the SAME sensor/viewpoint, and coverage holds in expectation over the calibration draw (inflate per Vovk 2012 for a PAC/training-conditional version).

Q1 temporal granularity: a per-frame bound union-bounded over a 10 Hz x 60 s episode (600 frames) is vacuous; a LATCHED trigger (once human ever enters the set, the track is human forever) makes the single-frame bound a legitimate per-track bound.

Q2 the hole is confirmed: Timans ECCV 2024 filters calibration to IoU-matched true-positive pairs — the two-step construction covers misCLASSIFICATION of detected boxes, never misDETECTION — so an occluded unseen pedestrian is outside every certificate, and occlusion grows with density, directly contradicting the crowding headline.

Q2 ranking: recall=1 is indefensible at RA-L; conformalized FN is really a density-stratified Clopper–Pearson binomial UCB needing annotated crowded data from the same onboard viewpoint (SDD bird's-eye does not transfer to a D435i) and occlusion is temporally correlated so repeated looks cannot redeem it; the geometric patch (unobserved space = adversarially occupied, occlusion shadows inflated by v_ped_max * t, never outrun your observed free space) is the most defensible — deterministic, zero statistical budget, and reuses the existing depth-to-occupancy pipeline; pure scoping-to-detected-agents matches community norms (Lindemann/Dixit assume observed agents) but guts the whole-chain headline.

Q3: Gibbs–Candes ACI guarantees only |T^-1 * sum(err_t) − eps| <= C/(gamma*T) — a deterministic bound on TIME-AVERAGED miscoverage over the realized sequence, no per-instant validity, recoverable by emitting trivial sets — so inside a safety theorem it quietly changes the bound's meaning; Dixit et al. L4DC 2023 are upfront theirs is the average-coverage form paired with MPC recursive feasibility and do NOT claim per-episode collision probability under shift — follow that precedent: formal bound from class-x-density Mondrian strata, ACI as empirical belt-and-suspenders only.

Q4: the union bound is correct under arbitrary dependence — the flaw is missing EVENTS, not the inequality; chain audit: detect-FN uncovered (the hole), associate UNBUDGETED (tubes calibrated on clean ground-truth SDD tracks but deployed on tracker-corrupted histories breaks exchangeability — fix by calibrating on tracker outputs end-to-end, which absorbs eps_assoc into eps_pred), classify covered, predict covered but needs a trajectory-level max-residual score (Cleaveland et al.) to avoid H-fold horizon union AND a K-fold union over pedestrians — the budget grows with crowd size, a second unacknowledged way density bites.

Q4 execution side: post-hoc verification + fallback validly absorbs everything DOWNSTREAM of the tubes (solver failure, infeasibility, numerics) and NOTHING upstream — the verifier consumes the same possibly-wrong world model; the vertical-climb backup genuinely escapes ground-bound pedestrian tubes but climbs into space the forward-facing D435i has never observed, so its recursive-feasibility proof depends on the Q2 unknown-space treatment; tracking error is fine if handled as measured margin inflation stated as an assumption.

Q5: stating performativity as a limitation is defensible by direct precedent — Lindemann et al. 2023 explicitly assume non-reactive agents, Dixit et al. partly motivate ACI by interaction-induced shift while still claiming only average coverage, and newer work (Who Moved My Distribution?, arXiv 2511.11567) now targets it — but it must be a NAMED assumption in the theorem statement, not a buried paragraph; a cheap disarm is an empirical tube-coverage check with reactive consenting subjects in the cage.

Overall: the composition is additively fixable (add eps_fn deterministic-or-bounded and eps_assoc via end-to-end calibration) — the required fix is honesty and two extra terms, not a new proof architecture.
numbers: Conditional miss rate under marginal-only calibration: up to eps/pi_human = 0.05/0.10 = 50% of real humans missed while marginal coverage 95% holds

Per-stratum calibration floor: n >= 1/eps − 1 = 19 samples minimum for eps=0.05 nontrivial quantile; coverage std ~ sqrt(eps(1−eps)/n) -> n ~= 475 per stratum for +/−1%; 4 density bins x human class ~= 1900+ labeled human detections
Episode union without latching: 10 Hz x 60 s = 600 frames -> 600 * eps_cls vacuous for any eps_cls > 0.0017
Multi-agent union: K=10 pedestrians x eps_pred=0.05 = 0.5 (vacuous) for collision-with-ANY-human; claim must be per-agent or budget split eps_pred/K
ACI guarantee form: |T^-1 * sum(err_t) − eps| <= (alpha_range)/(gamma*T) — time-average only, no statement about any fixed t
Occlusion shadow inflation for deterministic FN branch: r_shadow(t) = r_occluded + v_ped_max * t (v_ped_max ~ 1.5–2 m/s walking, ~4 m/s worst case)
Honest budget: eps_total = eps_fn(deterministic: 0) + eps_assoc(absorbed via end-to-end calibration) + eps_cls + K * eps_pred
risks: Reviewer-pool risk: Lindemann/Kantaros/Dixit reviewers will spot the FN conditioning gap immediately — it is the first question this community asks of any perception-side conformal claim; an overclaiming abstract is a likely reject even with good experiments.

Calibration-transfer risk: SDD is bird's-eye, the deployment sensor is an onboard forward-facing D435i — nonconformity scores calibrated on SDD detections/tracks are not exchangeable with onboard detections in any stratum; calibration data must come from the same sensor pipeline (Isaac Sim onboard renders or cage recordings), or this is a second silent exchangeability break.

Sample-size risk: class x density Mondrian multiplies strata while dividing calibration data; thin human-class bins in the high-density stratum (the one that matters) give wide beta-distributed coverage fluctuation — report per-stratum n or reviewers will.

Conservatism risk: the deterministic occlusion branch plus K-fold tube union in dense crowds may freeze the planner — the empirical price of the honest theorem could erase the performance story; budget evaluation time for this trade-off.
Timeline risk: 3 months zero buffer cannot fit FN handling + end-to-end tracker calibration + two-planner RTA demo; the second planner is the only cuttable item that does not touch the theorem.
analyses.detail:
Q1. Marginal coverage P(Y in C(X)) >= 1−eps gives P(Y=human, human not in C(X)) <= eps because that joint event is contained in the miscoverage event — so the literal asked-for inequality follows. But it is the wrong guarantee for a safety paper: (a) coverage can concentrate on abundant easy classes, so the conditional miss rate P(trigger fails | human) can be eps/pi_human; (b) sparse-to-crowded is label-prior shift, and marginal calibration is not invariant to it. The correct object is class-conditional (Mondrian) coverage: calibrate the score threshold on human-only calibration examples; the guarantee P(human in C(X) | Y=human) >= 1−eps_cls then holds under within-class exchangeability and is invariant to label shift — which is exactly the right property for the density-shift story and should be stated as such. Requirements: per-stratum human sample counts (Beta-distributed realized coverage; Vovk-2012-style inflation for training-conditional claims), same-sensor calibration data, and a latched per-track trigger so the per-frame guarantee composes to a per-track event without a 600-fold union.

Q2. Verified: Timans et al. (ECCV 2024 oral, arXiv 2403.07263) calibrate on matched true-positive box pairs; their two-step extends validity across misclassified detected objects, not undetected ones. The certificate is conditional on detection, FN rate climbs with occlusion/density, and the headline regime is therefore exactly where the certificate is silent. Recall=1 will not pass review. Conformalizing FN is really a binomial UCB (Clopper–Pearson) per density bin — needs presence-annotated crowded data in the deployment viewpoint, and occluded-person FN events are temporally persistent, so multi-frame redemption arguments fail. The geometric branch is strongest: treat unobserved/occluded space as adversarially occupied by agents with speed cap v_ped_max (phantom-agent/reachable-shadow construction), never commit into space you cannot stop short of — deterministic, additive, no budget, and the depth-occupancy pipeline plus the free-z climb already support it. Recommended: hybrid — deterministic branch for undetected humans + scoped statistical branch for detected ones + density-stratified empirical recall validation as evidence, with the scoping visible in the theorem statement and abstract.

Q3. ACI (Gibbs–Candes 2021) guarantees only that empirical miscoverage frequency over the realized sequence converges to eps at rate 1/(gamma*T), for arbitrary sequences, partly by inflating sets after errors; there is no per-time validity and no per-episode probability statement. A safety theorem quoting eps_pred from ACI has changed the meaning of the bound from a probability of a hitting event to an ergodic average — and density shift makes miscoverage cluster in dense (dangerous) intervals while sparse intervals pay it back. Dixit et al. (L4DC 2023, arXiv 2212.00278) are the honest precedent: they present ACI uncertainty sets with average-coverage semantics inside an MPC with recursive feasibility, and do not claim a per-episode collision bound under shift. The paper should derive the formal bound from class-x-density Mondrian strata (stated within-stratum exchangeability assumption — this IS contribution 1, and it is enough) and use ACI only as an empirical adaptation mechanism labeled time-average.

Q4. Union bound under arbitrary dependence: correct, always. The audit: detect (FN uncovered — the hole; FP is safe-side), associate (unbudgeted; tubes calibrated on ground-truth tracks but fed tracker histories at deployment breaks exchangeability; fix = calibrate the residuals on the SAME tracker's outputs, absorbing association noise into eps_pred while still conditioning on track existence), classify (covered per Q1), predict (covered; use trajectory-level max-residual scores per Cleaveland et al. to avoid horizon unions; K-agent union grows the budget with density — acknowledge or claim per-agent), plan/solve (validly absorbed by post-hoc verification + fallback), verify (deterministic given tubes; cannot absorb upstream perception error), execute (margin inflation by measured tracking bound, stated as assumption). The climb fallback is sound against ground-bound tubes only if the unknown-space-above problem inherits the Q2 deterministic treatment.

Q5. Defensible as a named assumption with precedent (Lindemann et al. 2023 non-reactive-agents assumption; Dixit et al. motivate ACI by interaction shift; arXiv 2511.11567 now attacks it directly — cite it). Add an empirical coverage-under-reaction check in the cage to disarm.

verified.verdict: The pivot is mathematically viable, but ONLY as a per-detected-track, per-planning-episode guarantee with explicit deterministic branches — not as the headlined "P(collision with a human) <= eps_cls + eps_pred covering the whole chain." (i) Viable: every key number in both analyses recomputes correctly; the budget closes at eps=0.1 (eps_cls=0.02, eps_pred=0.08). (ii) Scoring design: per-agent time-shaped functional score s_i = max_t ||e_t||/rho(t) calibrated end-to-end on tracker-output histories (absorbing association error), one scored window per track (no overlapping windows), union bound only over agents (alpha_cell = eps_pred/H_bin), class-conditional (human-only) classification threshold with a latched first-detection trigger, Mondrian = {human, vehicle-like, other} x {H<=1, 3, 10} = 9 cells; undetected/occluded humans covered by a deterministic reachable-shadow branch (r_occ + v_max*t), visible-but-unclassified humans by the existing deterministic body-clearance floor inflated by replan latency (~0.4 m). (iii) Sample sizes: minimum 12/37/124 trajectories per human-class density cell, ~1,250 comfortable in the crowded cell, ~5,250 total for 9 cells; ~200-500 labeled human first-detections per density stratum for classification — all calibrated in Isaac Sim onboard renders or cage recordings, NOT on SDD (bird's-eye-to-D435i viewpoint shift breaks exchangeability; SDD is for predictor training only). (iv) Must weaken: per-timestep -> per-encounter; per-mission -> per-episode; "whole chain" -> three-branch scoping stated in the theorem; the "arbitrary correlation" theorem is a one-line union bound (valid, not the novelty); "sparse-to-crowded" -> within calibrated density bins up to H_max=10; ACI demoted to an empirical time-average adaptation layer; constant-velocity prediction must be replaced (it is the binding constraint: 2.0 m vs 0.9 m terminal tubes = blocked vs passable 4 m corridor); if the 3-month timeline forces a cut, cut the second-planner demo, never the FN handling.
key_points: VERIFIED: all arithmetic in both analyses reproduces exactly — union-bound alphas, n_min = ceil(1/alpha - 1) from rank ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)) <= n, Mondrian multiplications, lognormal quantiles, and the at-n_min-quantile-equals-sample-maximum property all check out; no wrong finite-sample rule anywhere.

SURVIVES (A1): the naive per-(agent,timestep) design is dead — alpha = 1.33e-4 at (H=10, T=30, eps_pred=0.04) needs n_min = 7,499 per cell (67k-1.35M with Mondrian) and, under the stated lognormal model, ~4.6 m tubes (4.0x the 95% radius) that certify permanent infeasibility in a 4 m corridor.

SURVIVES (A1): minimum viable design is the per-agent time-shaped max-over-horizon score with alpha = eps_pred/H (124 min / 1,250 comfortable trajectories per crowded human cell at eps_pred=0.08), and the circularity critique of scene-level max-over-agents scoring (it manufactures the density-shift collapse that contribution 1 then fixes) will land with Pappas-lineage reviewers.

SURVIVES (A2, the deepest point): missed detections are outside every conformal certificate in the chain (Timans ECCV 2024 calibrates on IoU-matched true positives), FN rises with the headlined density shift, so eps_cls + eps_pred cannot bound P(collision) as stated — the fix is a deterministic occlusion branch (unobserved space adversarially occupied with speed cap), not a statistical budget.

SURVIVES (both): ACI gives only deterministic time-average miscoverage |T^-1 sum err_t - eps| <= C/(gamma T) and permits miscoverage to concentrate in dense moments — it cannot appear inside the finite-sample headline; demote to empirical adaptation layer (Dixit L4DC 2023 is the honest precedent).

WRONG (A1): the budget P(hit) <= eps_cls + eps_pred with execution ~0 is unprovable as stated because detection FN is acknowledged only as a risk, never budgeted — Analysis 2's three-term restatement (deterministic FN branch + assoc absorbed + cls + pred) is the correct theorem skeleton.

WRONG (A1, minor): "n >= 99, classification never the bottleneck" uses the marginal minimum; the correct class-conditional (Mondrian-by-class) guarantee needs ~200-475 labeled human detections per density stratum from the deployment sensor (~1,900 total) — feasible but not free, and marginal-only calibration allows a 50% conditional miss rate on humans (eps/pi_human = 0.05/0.10).

SLIGHTLY OVERCLAIMED (A2): "eps_fn deterministic: 0" misses visible-but-undetected humans (not in any occlusion shadow); in THIS system they degrade to the existing depth-occupancy body-clearance floor (plan_minco.hpp:915-919 gate), which is deterministic but instantaneous — honest coverage needs a replan-latency inflation (0.1 s x 4 m/s = 0.4 m) and yields non-penetration at replan resolution, not predictive tubes; the theorem must state three perception branches explicitly.

MISSING FROM BOTH (prompt checklist item): overlapping sliding windows — extracting multiple overlapping 3 s windows per trajectory pseudo-replicates calibration samples and breaks joint exchangeability with a fresh test window; the unit must be one scored window per track (or non-overlapping with random offset), so the effective dataset is ~10^4 trajectories, not ~10^5 windows.

REFINEMENT (A2's latch): latching is sound (P(never trigger) <= P(no trigger at first detection)) but only if calibration uses the SAME designated unit — calibrate the human-conditional threshold on first-detection frames per track, since first detections (far, small, partially occluded) are covariate-shifted relative to random frames.

SURVIVES (A2): SDD-calibrate / onboard-D435i-deploy is a fatal exchangeability break for the certificate (bird's-eye vs forward-facing onboard); calibrate in Isaac Sim onboard renders or cage recordings, use SDD only to train the predictor.

BINDING CONSTRAINT (A1, conditional on its lognormal model): the predictor, not the conformal machinery — CV gives 2.0 m terminal tubes (blocked band 5.0 m > 4 m corridor, one pedestrian closes it) vs 0.9 m learned (2.8 m band, passable); note these radii are modeled assumptions to be validated on real residuals, not established facts.
TIMELINE: both analyses agree the only cuttable item that does not touch the theorem is the second-planner RTA demo; FN handling and end-to-end tracker calibration are not cuttable.
numbers: Naive union: alpha = eps_pred/(H*T) = 0.04/300 = 1.333e-4; n_min = ceil(1/alpha - 1) = 7,499 (verified; rank at n=7,499 equals n, i.e., quantile = calibration maximum)

Non-vacuity rule verified: ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)) <= n iff n >= 1/alpha - 1; boundary case alpha = 0.04/3 = 1/75, n = 74 holds EXACTLY ((n+1)(1-alpha) = 74) — naive float evaluation gives 74.000000000000006 -> implementation must compute the rank in exact arithmetic

Mondrian totals: 3 classes x {1,3,10} bins = 519 min / 5,250 comfortable (eps_pred = 0.08); 1,041 / 10,500 (eps_pred = 0.04); naive x Mondrian = 7,499 x 9 = 67,491 min, 75,000 x 18 = 1.35M — infeasible
Corridor: blocked band = 2(r + 0.5 m) = 5.0 m (CV) vs 2.8 m (learned) vs 4 m corridor width
Classification: n_min = 1/0.02 - 1 = 49 at eps_cls = 0.02; +/-1% coverage stability needs n ~ eps(1-eps)/1e-4 = 196 (eps=0.02) to 475 (eps=0.05) per stratum; ~1,900 human detections over 4 strata
Conditional miss under marginal-only calibration: eps/pi_human = 0.05/0.10 = 50%
Frame union without latching: 600 frames x eps_cls vacuous for eps_cls > 1/600 = 1.67e-3; K-agent union: 10 x 0.05 = 0.5 (vacuous)
Visible-unclassified latency margin: 0.1 s replan x 4 m/s worst-case pedestrian = 0.4 m body-floor inflation; occlusion shadow r(t) = r_occ + v_max * t
risks: All tube-radius and corridor-feasibility numbers ride on an assumed lognormal residual model fitted to two quantiles; real pedestrian residuals (stops, reversals, ID switches) can be heavier-tailed, and at n near n_min the deployed quantile IS the calibration maximum — one outlier inflates every tube.

The honest three-branch theorem (statistical tubes + occlusion shadows + body floor) may be so conservative in dense scenes that the planner freezes — the performance story can die even when the math survives; budget evaluation time for this trade-off explicitly.

Pappas-lineage reviewers will ask the FN-conditioning question first and the marginal-vs-conditional question second; an abstract that promises whole-chain or per-timestep coverage is a likely reject regardless of experiments.

Contribution (1) as currently framed (coverage collapse diagnosis) partially dissolves under per-agent scoring — it must be reframed as class-conditional + density-stratified calibration with an explicit H union, which is a weaker but defensible novelty.

3 months zero buffer cannot fit FN handling + end-to-end tracker calibration + learned predictor + two-planner demo; the predictor upgrade and FN branch are both load-bearing, so the schedule realistically forces dropping the second planner AND scoping real flights down.
Per-stratum effective n is further reduced by same-scene agent correlation even after fixing the windowing — report effective per-cell counts or reviewers will compute them.
verified.detail:
RECOMPUTATION (all via Python, exact arithmetic where boundary-sensitive). (1) Naive alphas eps_pred/(H*T) and n_min = ceil(1/alpha - 1): every entry in Analysis 1's tables reproduces (499/749/1499/2249/4999/7499 at eps_pred=0.04; halved-alpha column at 0.08 likewise). The non-vacuity derivation is the correct split-conformal rule: rank ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)) <= n iff n >= (1-alpha)/alpha; verified numerically that at n = n_min the rank equals n (quantile = sample max) and at n_min - 1 the set is vacuous. One boundary case (alpha = 1/75, n = 74) fails in floating point but holds exactly — an implementation footnote, not an analysis error. (2) Per-agent design: alpha = eps_pred/H gives n_min = {12, 37, 124} and comfortable = {125, 375, 1,250} at eps_pred = 0.08; Mondrian totals 519/1,041 minimum and 5,250/10,500 comfortable for 3 classes (the analyses' "10x" is 10/alpha, internally consistent); naive x Mondrian 67,491-1.35M confirmed infeasible. (3) Lognormal radii: sigma = ln(3)/1.6449 = 0.668 reproduces r(0.008) = 2.00, r(1.33e-4) = 4.57, ratio 4.0; learned-predictor sigma = 0.532 gives r(0.008) = 0.90. These are MODEL outputs, not data. (4) Analysis 2's numbers (0.5 conditional miss, n = 19, 475 for +/-1%, 1/600 threshold, K-union 0.5) all check.

ERROR HUNT against the prompt's checklist. Wrong finite-sample rule: none found. Exchangeability-unit mismatches: three real ones — (a) SDD bird's-eye vs onboard D435i (fatal for certificate calibration; both analyses flag, A2 correctly makes it disqualifying); (b) calibrating tubes on ground-truth histories but deploying on tracker outputs (A2's end-to-end fix is correct and absorbs eps_assoc); (c) NEW: the latched classification trigger needs calibration on the same designated unit (first detection per track), since first detections are covariate-shifted vs random frames. Overlapping sliding windows: addressed by NEITHER analysis explicitly — overlapping 3 s windows from one trajectory pseudo-replicate samples and break joint exchangeability with a fresh test window; mandate one scored window per track, making the honest dataset ~10^4 units, which the surviving design still fits at eps = 0.1 (5,250 comfortable) but not at eps = 0.05 with 6 classes (21,000). Marginal vs class-conditional: A2's correction stands; A1's "never the bottleneck" understates the per-stratum human-labeled requirement (~200-475/stratum) but the conclusion (not the binding constraint) survives. ACI: both correctly identify the time-average semantics; quoting it in the headline would change the bound's mathematical object from a hitting-event probability to an ergodic average that can concentrate failures in dense intervals. Missing chain links: detect-FN is the structural hole (A1 lists it as a risk but leaves it out of the budget — that makes A1's headline budget unprovable as stated; A2's deterministic shadow branch is the fix); A2's "eps_fn = 0" is itself slightly overclaimed for visible-but-undetected humans, which in this specific system fall back to the deterministic depth-occupancy body-penetration gate (plan_minco.hpp:915-919) — deterministic but instantaneous, requiring a ~0.4 m replan-latency inflation and yielding only non-penetration-at-replan-resolution, so the theorem must name three perception branches; replan-cycle union (600/min) and per-frame classification union are real and handled by per-episode restatement + latching; the vertical-climb backup's recursive feasibility correctly inherits the unknown-space-above treatment (A2 right — the D435i is forward-facing).

SYNTHESIS. Analysis 1 wins on the epsilon arithmetic and scoring-design selection (design (d) is the certificate core; escape (c) is correctly identified as circular; Cleaveland/CopulaCPTS correctly demoted to baselines). Analysis 2 wins on theorem structure (FN hole, class-conditional correction, latching, end-to-end tracker calibration, ACI semantics, named assumptions including non-reactive pedestrians with Lindemann-precedent cover). The two are compatible: A2's theorem skeleton + A1's budget numbers + the three additions above (windowing rule, first-detection latch calibration, body-floor latency branch) = the publishable object. Final budget: eps = 0.1, eps_cls = 0.02 (latched, class-conditional, per-track), eps_pred = 0.08 (per-agent tubes, explicit union over H <= 10, end-to-end on tracker outputs), FN/occlusion/execution deterministic. eps = 0.05 only at H <= 3 or merged bins. The single highest-leverage engineering item remains replacing constant-velocity prediction — the entire gap between meaningful (0.9 m) and vacuous (2.0 m+) tubes lives in the predictor's q95, not in the conformal machinery.

sweeps.verdict: All four anchor works plus the reference design are real and now verified from primary sources, and none of them combines class-conditional/semantic risk with dynamic agents and closed-loop control: Strawn et al. (RA-L 2023), Dixit et al. (L4DC 2023) and Lindemann et al. (RA-L 2023) all do dynamic agents + control but are completely class-blind (one uniform safety distance for every agent, no perception in the loop); the Conformalized Semantic Maps paper (Sundarsingh et al., arXiv 2509.25124, accepted to an IEEE letters journal, almost certainly RA-L 2026) has class-dependent margins but a strictly static world and a guarantee that is joint, not class-conditional; Timans et al. (ECCV 2024) is perception-only with no dynamics or control and explicitly excludes missed detections. The triple intersection (semantic per-class risk + moving agents + control) is open across all five — a defensible gap, with the caveat that Kalluraya/Pappas/Kantaros' "Multi-robot mission planning in dynamic semantic environments" (arXiv 2209.06323, non-conformal) is the nearest neighbor and should be cited when claiming it.
key_points: (a) resolves to Strawn, Ayanian, Lindemann, 'Conformal Predictive Safety Filter for RL Controllers in Dynamic Environments', IEEE RA-L 2023 (DOI 10.1109/LRA.2023.3322644, arXiv:2306.02551) — it is NOT a drone paper: experiments are a 2D collision-avoidance gym with ground-truth agent states, no perception, no semantic classes.

Strawn's safety guarantee is conditional on the learned neural filter actually satisfying the CP constraints, which are only enforced approximately via unconstrained penalty training — it is not an end-to-end certificate.

(b) resolves to Sundarsingh, Li, Tang, Pappas, Atanasov, Kantaros, 'Safe Planning in Unknown Environments using Conformalized Semantic Maps' (arXiv:2509.25124; IEEE Xplore 11417450 with RA-L-style editorial note): class-dependent safe distances in a STATIC environment; the CP guarantee is joint over all cells/classes, NOT class-conditional, and dynamic agents are entirely out of scope.

(c) Timans, Straehle, Sakmann, Nalisnick, 'Adaptive Bounding Box Uncertainties via Two-Step Conformal Prediction', ECCV 2024 Oral (arXiv:2403.07263): calibrates on Hungarian-matched true positives (IoU>=0.5); step 1 = conformal class-label set, step 2 = box intervals using the max quantile over labels in that set; missed detections (false negatives) are explicitly declared out of scope.

(d) Dixit, Lindemann, Wei, Cleaveland, Pappas, Burdick, L4DC 2023 (PMLR v211, pp. 300-314): ACP buys online quantile adaptation from a single trajectory stream — no offline calibration set, no exchangeability, distribution may depend on ego state x — but the price is a weaker AVERAGE-over-time coverage guarantee (Theorem 7), not pointwise; deterministic single ego system, one generic obstacle (frisbee vs multirotor), no classes, no perception.

(e) Lindemann, Cleaveland, Shim, Pappas, RA-L 2023 (vol. 8 no. 8, pp. 5116-5123, arXiv:2210.10254): nonconformity score is PER-TIME-STEP error R_tau|t = ||Y_tau - Yhat_tau|t|| with per-step regions combined across the horizon via Boole's inequality at delta_bar = delta/T — i.e., per-step union bound, NOT a max-over-horizon score; the only max in the paper (Remark 2) is over AGENTS, not time.

Lindemann et al.'s own conclusion names the union-bound conservatism as future work ('induced by union bounding over events over several time steps in Theorem 1'), so a sibling analysis premised on the per-step-union design is correct; one premised on max-over-horizon would be wrong.

No paper among the five combines class-conditional/semantic risk + dynamic agents + control: (a)(d)(e) are class-blind dynamic control, (b) is semantic but static and not class-conditional, (c) is perception-only.
numbers: Strawn RA-L 2023: collisions -80% (vs GA3C-CADRL), timeouts -67% (vs ORCA), paths -18% vs Gaussian filter; delta = 0.01, H = 7 steps, N in {2,4,6} agents; CPSF-GA3C empirical interval coverage = 99%

Lindemann RA-L 2023: delta_bar = delta/T (Bonferroni); region C_tau|t = p-th smallest score with p = ceil((|D_cal|+1)(1-delta_bar)); CARLA: 1 violation / 100 runs vs <=5 allowed (delta=0.05, T=30); one-step empirical coverage 99.985% vs 99.83% required

Dixit L4DC 2023: average coverage bound = 1 - delta - p1 with p1 = (delta_0^1 + gamma)/(T*gamma) -> 0; at delta=0.025: feasibility 83.8% (ACP) vs 97.1% (EKF), mean min-distance 2.91 m (ACP) vs 14.2 m (bootstrap) vs 5.27 m (EKF) — tighter by ~2-5x
Timans ECCV 2024: TP matching threshold IoU >= 0.5; box quantile q^B = max over labels y in conformal label set C_L of class-conditional quantile q^B_y
Conformalized Semantic Maps: class-dependent margins example d_person = 4 m, d_car = 1 m, d_tree = 0.5 m; map prediction sets contain ground truth w.p. >= 1 - alpha (joint, user-specified)
risks: (b)'s venue is inferred: IEEE Xplore blocked direct fetch (HTTP 418), so 'RA-L 2026' rests on the Xplore listing (doc 11417450, appeared ~Feb 2026) plus the RA-L-format editorial note ('recommended for publication by Editor Lucia Pallottino', an RA-L senior editor); volume/issue/pages unconfirmed — verify before citing in a camera-ready.

Calling (a) a 'drone runtime-assurance/conformal-shield' paper in the manuscript would mischaracterize it: it is a 2D gym RL safety filter (the gym's policies were transferred to aerial robots in PRIOR work by Everett et al., not in this paper), and its guarantee is conditional on the learned filter's constraint satisfaction.

For (e), the published RA-L version corresponds to arXiv v2 (8 Jun 2023); the union-bound conservatism was later reduced in follow-up work (Cleaveland et al., LCP-based time-series CP regions) — if the sibling analysis contrasts against 'the union bound', it should cite the RA-L paper, not the follow-up, and not conflate them.

Novelty claim risk: Kalluraya, Pappas & Kantaros (arXiv 2209.06323) does dynamic SEMANTIC environments with mission planning (non-conformal), and COPPOL (arXiv 2510.18485) does conformalized segmentation with missed-detection bounds for RL navigation — neither closes the triple gap, but both narrow it and should be positioned against.
sweeps.detail:
(a) Strawn. Exact title: "Conformal Predictive Safety Filter for RL Controllers in Dynamic Environments". Authors: Kegan J. Strawn, Nora Ayanian, Lars Lindemann. Venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 2023 (DOI 10.1109/LRA.2023.3322644; arXiv:2306.02551v2). Core claim: for a pre-trained RL policy, train a neural "predictive safety filter" that imitates the RL controller while avoiding conformal uncertainty intervals around LSTM-predicted agent trajectories; per-step split-CP intervals C_{t+h}, h=1..H with delta_bar = delta/T (Bonferroni, following Lindemann et al.). Does NOT cover: perception (ground-truth agent states), semantic classes (all agents share one radius epsilon=0.5), real hardware, distribution shift (Assumption 1; argues empirically shifts are small), hard certificates (filter trained by unconstrained penalty, guarantee holds "under the assumption that the safety filter achieves the objective in (7)"). Stated future work: test the filter on non-RL controllers, verify modularity (swap policies), and apply adaptive CP to relax assumptions when distribution shifts occur in D.

(b) Conformalized Semantic Maps. Exact title: "Safe Planning in Unknown Environments using Conformalized Semantic Maps". Authors: David Smith Sundarsingh, Yifei Li, Tianji Tang, George J. Pappas, Nikolay Atanasov, Yiannis Kantaros. Venue: arXiv:2509.25124 (Sep 2025, rev. Feb 2026); accepted IEEE letters journal per editorial header (RA-L editor Lucia Pallottino), Xplore doc 11417450 — treat as RA-L 2026 pending confirmation. Core claim: first planner for semantic reach-avoid achieving user-specified mission completion rates with no sensor/noise model: CP produces sets of semantic maps containing the true environment w.p. >= 1-alpha; closed-loop replanning (Algorithm 2) with class-dependent distances (person 4 m, car 1 m, tree 0.5 m). Does NOT cover: dynamic agents (regions "fixed over time"), class-conditional guarantees (Prop. IV.1 is joint over all cells/classes), continuous dynamics control. Future work: active exploration to shrink prediction sets, robust CP for out-of-distribution, sensor-level rather than map-level UQ.

(c) Timans. Exact title: "Adaptive Bounding Box Uncertainties via Two-Step Conformal Prediction". Authors: Alexander Timans, Christoph-Nikolas Straehle, Kaspar Sakmann, Eric Nalisnick. Venue: ECCV 2024 (Oral; Springer LNCS, arXiv:2403.07263; code alextimans/conformal-od). Scope confirmed: box-coordinate intervals calibrated ONLY on detections Hungarian-matched to ground truth at IoU>=0.5 (true positives); step 1 builds a conformal class-label set (ClassThr), step 2 takes per-coordinate class-conditional quantiles and uses the max over labels in the set (q^B = max_{y in C_L} q^B_y), so box coverage survives misclassification — guarantee is label-set-marginalized, not strictly class-conditional. Missed detections explicitly out of scope: "guarantees only hold for true objects that are actually detected (true positives) and do not account for undetected objects (false negatives), as also noted by Andeol et al." No planner/controller — collision avoidance and grasping appear only as motivation.

(d) Dixit. Exact title: "Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Motion Planning among Dynamic Agents". Authors: Anushri Dixit*, Lars Lindemann*, Skylar X. Wei, Matthew Cleaveland, George J. Pappas, Joel W. Burdick (*equal). Venue: L4DC 2023, PMLR v211, pp. 300-314 (arXiv:2212.00278). What ACP buys: online update delta_{t+1} = delta_t + gamma(delta - e_t) of the quantile from a single observed trajectory — removes the offline calibration dataset and exchangeability assumptions of (e), tolerates D depending on ego state x (interaction-induced shift). Price: guarantee degrades from pointwise to time-averaged coverage (Theorem 7: (1/T) sum Prob(c>=0) >= 1-delta-p1, p1 -> 0), proven only via one-step-ahead errors; multistep regions use a time-lagged score R_t^tau = ||Y_t - Yhat^tau_{t-tau}|| under an extra iid-like heuristic. Assumes deterministic single-ego dynamics, Lipschitz constraint, generic agents (joint state R^{Nn}), no classes, no perception; case study = one multirotor vs one frisbee. Stated limitation/future work: MPC feasibility drops (83.8% vs 97.1% for EKF) from sudden region-size jumps at large gamma; plan recursive-feasibility tools (Hewing et al.) or backup controllers.

(e) Lindemann. Exact title: "Safe Planning in Dynamic Environments Using Conformal Prediction". Authors: Lars Lindemann*, Matthew Cleaveland*, Gihyun Shim, George J. Pappas. Venue: IEEE RA-L vol. 8, no. 8, pp. 5116-5123, 2023 (arXiv:2210.10254v2). Nonconformity design CONFIRMED: per-step score R^(i)_{tau|t} = ||Y^(i)_tau - Yhat^(i)_{tau|t}|| on the joint agent state; Lemma 1 gives per-step regions C_{tau|t} = p-th smallest score, p = ceil((|D_cal|+1)(1-delta_bar)); Theorem 1 sets delta_bar := delta/T and union-bounds (Boole) across tau = 1..T. It is per-step + union bound, not max-over-horizon; Remark 2's max is over agents j only (per-agent circles). Conclusion explicitly lists as future work: adaptive methods to cut the union-bound conservatism, handling arbitrary numbers of agents, predictor-MPC interplay study; Remark 4 defers distribution shift to robust CP. No classes (single epsilon for all pedestrians), ground-truth states, fixed N.

Combination check: none of the five (nor any work found alongside them) provides class-conditional/semantic risk + dynamic agents + control simultaneously; nearest neighbors to cite when claiming the gap: Kalluraya/Pappas/Kantaros arXiv 2209.06323 (dynamic semantic, non-conformal) and COPPOL arXiv 2510.18485 (conformal segmentation with FN bounds, static hazards).

sweeps.verdict: No 2024-2026 work closes the full claimed gap. Every single component (i)-(iv) now exists somewhere in isolation or in pairs, and two pairs are getting crowded fast — conformal semantic-class-dependent margins (Kantaros/Pappas/Atanasov, RA-L 2026) covers most of (i) for static maps, and density-parameterized robust CP planning (Lindemann group, Feb 2026) covers the core of (iii) — but nobody composes conformal CLASSIFICATION label sets with conformal trajectory-prediction tubes into one end-to-end P(collision) bound, nobody stratifies conformal calibration by class x crowd-density (Mondrian), nobody enforces such a bound via a monitor + minimal-correction-QP + backup RTA stack, and nobody demonstrates any conformal safety layer across multiple planners. The combination is genuinely unclaimed, but the window is closing: the Kantaros/Pappas/Atanasov and Lindemann pipelines each hold 3-4 of the 5 ingredients, so the defensible kernel — (i)+(ii) composed in one certificate, hardened with class x density stratification — realistically stays open ~6-12 months; the (iv)+(v) packaging alone is not defensible and should not be the headline claim.
key_points: Closest hit to (i): 'Safe Planning in Unknown Environments using Conformalized Semantic Maps' (arXiv 2509.25124, RA-L 2026; Sundarsingh, Li, Tang, Pappas, Atanasov, Kantaros) conformalizes semantic labels and enforces CLASS-DEPENDENT distances with a user-specified mission-success guarantee — but static environments only, no pedestrians/tubes, no RTA, single planner.

Closest hit to planner-agnostic end-to-end bound: 'Perceive With Confidence' (arXiv 2403.08185, Majumdar group, rev. 2025) conformalizes detection/scene-completion and claims any-safe-planner composability with an end-to-end statistical assurance — but static obstacles only and demonstrated on one planner.

Component (ii) is the most crowded: Lindemann/Pappas 2210.10254 lineage plus 2502.06221 (interaction-aware crowd CP), 2511.18170 (SIPP + adaptive CP), SPARC 2410.15660, conformal predictive safety filters — conformal pedestrian tubes alone carry zero novelty in 2026.

Component (iii) is being closed right now: 'When Environments Shift' (arXiv 2602.12616, Feb 2026, Lindemann) explicitly handles traffic-DENSITY-parameterized shift with robust CP + MPC guarantees; CoRL 2025 crowd-nav (2508.05634) handles individual-to-group shift empirically; only the Mondrian class-x-density stratification specifically remains unclaimed (Mondrian CP just entered robotics via 2603.08958 but stratified by formation/state region, not class x density).

Component (iv) pairs with CP are emerging monthly: ensembles of safety filters + CP (2511.07899), cost-aware adaptive conformal inference for runtime assurance (2605.24463, May 2026), conformal flight-test monitoring (2511.20811), conformal safety shielding with a composed global safety bound (2506.17275, RV 2025) — but the exact monitor + minimal-correction QP + backup-maneuver triplet fed by conformal sets does not exist as a unit.

Component (v) — demonstration across MULTIPLE planners — is claimed in principle only (Perceive With Confidence); no paper found actually evaluates one conformal safety layer across several planners, but this alone is weak novelty (reviewers may call it 'just evaluation').

The genuinely unclaimed kernel is the COMPOSITION: one end-to-end P(collision) bound that multiplies/unions conformal classification sets (gating hard-vs-soft constraint hardness) with conformal prediction tubes, calibrated per class x density — no paper from the Lindemann, Kantaros, Atanasov, or Pappas 2025-2026 output does this.

Honest window estimate: 6-12 months for the (i)+(ii)+(iii) kernel — a dynamic-obstacle sequel to 2509.25124 or a classification extension of 2602.12616 is the natural next paper from groups that already have all ingredients; the RTA packaging and multi-planner evaluation add maybe 6 more months of defensive moat but cannot stand alone.

Per-hit list (title / venue / year — components covered of (i) classification-gated hardness, (ii) pedestrian CP tubes, (iii) density-shift robustness, (iv) RTA monitor+QP+backup, (v) multi-planner):

10. Cost-Aware Adaptive Conformal Inference for Runtime Assurance — arXiv 2605.24463 (May 2026). (iii)+(iv): ACI under time-varying distributions bounding violation frequency and cumulative harm.

result.verdict: Pillar A (SDD) = viable with caveats: the 6 class labels exist and pedestrian/biker cells are comfortably powered (thousands of trajectories per density tercile), but cart (~200), bus (~100) and skater (~300) classes cannot support 3 density bins at 100-1000 scores/cell — merge them into a "vehicle"/"wheeled" superclass or drop to 2 bins; also SDD density is uniformly low (global <0.1 persons/m², coupa/bookstore <0.02), so the "high-density" bin is really "high-interaction campus intersection," and coordinates are pixels with only community-estimated scales. Pillar B (Isaac Sim people sim) = viable: the current Isaacsim Replicator Agent (IRA, successor of omni.anim.people) exposes a YAML key `groups[].num` for exact agent count (i.e., density is directly programmable), seeded deterministic spawning on navmesh areas, and per-frame ground truth including actor position/rotation/speed/task plus class-semantic segmentation, 2D/3D boxes and skeletons — ideal for oracle-perception experiments; the only soft spot is that NVIDIA documents no agent-count limit and community practice is tens of concurrent characters, with 100+ requiring workarounds.
key_points: SDD labels exactly the 6 classes asked about (pedestrian, bicyclist, skateboarder, cart, car, bus) over 8 scenes / 60 videos, ~19-20k unique targets, ~10.3k trajectories (24.9k 4.8s trajlets per OpenTraj).

Class counts are heavily skewed: ~11.2k pedestrians, ~6.4k bicyclists, ~1.3k cars, ~0.3k skateboarders, ~0.2k carts, ~0.1k buses — the bottom three classes are an order of magnitude too thin for class x 3-density conformal cells.

Scene-level density variation exists (deathCircle 2,830 trajectories vs quad 59; biker share 4-56%, car share 0-29.5% by scene) so ~3 bins by local neighbor count are constructible, but absolute density is low everywhere (global <0.1 p/m2), so SDD cannot give a true crowd-density bin.

Estimated per-cell counts (even tercile split, trajectory level): ped ~3.7k, biker ~2.1k, car ~430 (OK-marginal), skater ~100 (borderline), cart ~67 and bus ~33 (blocked); skew toward low-density bins makes top-bin cells for car/skater likely <100.

Known SDD issues confirmed: pixel coordinates with no official homography (OpenTraj/TrajNet++ provide approximate per-scene scales), 68-91% of trajectories contain 'lost' frames at start, interpolated/occluded flags, identity splits requiring manual cross-checking, and class quirks (a biker pushing a bike stays 'Biker').

Alternatives: ETH/UCY (peds only, ~1.8k agents, meters, too small); ATC mall (92 days, 49 3D sensors, ~900 m2, huge N and natural weekday/weekend density sweep, but no class labels); JRDB (peds only, 1.8M 3D cuboids, ~3.5k trajectories, robot-egocentric); THOR/THOR-Magni (small-N indoor mocap, role labels not vehicle classes); nuScenes (rich classes incl. pedestrian subtypes + vehicles, ~1.4M 3D boxes, but 20s driving scenes at 2 Hz keyframes, low crowd density); TrajNet++ (peds only, but its interaction-type categorization is a ready-made density/interaction binning).
Best patch for A: SDD with {pedestrian, biker, merged-vehicle} x 3 bins, plus ATC for the density axis (single class) — covers both axes without any single dataset doing both.

Isaac Sim: omni.anim.people is deprecated in favor of IRA (isaacsim.replicator.agent); IRA config takes character groups with required `num`, optional navmesh `spawn_areas`, 32-bit `seed` for deterministic spawn/routines, randomized or scripted commands (GoTo/wander/patrol), and headless SDG runs at 30 FPS playback.

result.detail:
Method: web verification against the SDD project page, the SDD-complexity analysis paper (arXiv 2203.11743), OpenTraj (ACCV 2020, arXiv 2010.00890), Isaac Sim 4.5/6.0 docs (IRA configuration + people simulation), and community repos.

(A) SDD. Classes: pedestrian, bicyclist, skateboarder, cart, car, bus — confirmed. Scale: 8 scenes (bookstore, coupa, deathCircle, gates, hyang, little, nexus, quad), 60 videos, ~19-20k annotated targets, ~10,300 trajectories; OpenTraj counts ~24,921 trajlets of 4.8s. Class skew: 11.2k ped / 6.4k biker / 1.3k car / 0.3k skater / 0.2k cart / 0.1k bus. Scene mix varies strongly (deathCircle 56.3% biker, nexus 29.5% car, quad 87.5% ped), and per-scene trajectory volume spans 59 (quad) to 2,830 (deathCircle), so 3 density bins by instantaneous neighbor count are constructible — but OpenTraj measures SDD global density <0.1 p/m2 (coupa/bookstore <0.02), i.e., no true high-density regime exists in SDD. Per-cell arithmetic (even tercile split at trajectory level): ped ~3.7k, biker ~2.1k OK; car ~433 marginal (and cars concentrate in nexus/deathCircle, rarely co-occurring with dense pedestrians, so the joint top-bin cell likely <100); skater ~100 borderline; cart ~67 and bus ~33 blocked for a 100-1000-scores-per-cell conformal recipe. Fix: merge car+cart+bus (~1.6k -> ~533/cell) or use 2 bins for minority classes. Known issues confirmed: pixel coordinates at 30 fps with no official homography (community scale files from OpenTraj/TrajNet++ are approximate); 'lost'/occluded/auto-interpolated flags pervasive (68-91% of trajectories contain lost frames at the start); identity splits; semantic label quirks (dismounted biker still 'Biker'). Alternatives: ETH/UCY — peds only, ~1.8k agents, metric, too small for cells; ATC — 92 days, 49 3D range sensors, ~900 m2 mall, enormous N with natural weekday/Sunday density sweep, but single class; JRDB — peds only, 1.8M 3D cuboids / ~3,500 trajectories, robot egocentric; THOR/THOR-Magni — mocap-accurate indoor, role labels (carrier/visitor) not agent classes, small N; nuScenes — real multi-class incl. pedestrian subtypes, ~1.4M 3D boxes, but 20s scenes at 2 Hz keyframes and driving viewpoint; TrajNet++ — peds only, but ships interaction-type categorization usable as a density-bin template.

(B) Isaac Sim. omni.anim.people is officially deprecated in favor of Isaacsim Replicator Agent (IRA). Density control is directly programmatic: config YAML `character.groups[].num` (>=0), optional navmesh `spawn_areas`, global 32-bit `seed` giving deterministic spawn locations and routine variation, command files/randomized commands (GoTo, wander, patrol), headless SDG at 30 FPS playback, robot agents in the same config. Ground truth fully covers oracle-perception needs: IRABasicWriter emits RGB, camera params, semantic segmentation (class labels per agent via semantics), bounding_box_2d_tight/loose, bounding_box_3d, depth, motion vectors, 2D/3D skeleton joints, and object_detection.json embeds per-frame actor position, rotation, speed and current task — i.e., exact world-frame trajectories with identities and classes without running a perception stack. Practical counts: NVIDIA publishes no ceiling; community evidence (SCAI-Lab/isaac-crowd-sim, which patches global_character_position_manager.py and exports JRDB-format trajectories; dillonloh/isaac-sim-people-cycle-sim built to recycle character prims for 'large amounts of human traffic') indicates tens of concurrent animated characters are routine and 100+ needs workarounds — sufficient for ~3 density tiers (e.g., 5/15/40 agents) in a courtyard-scale scene.

judges.rationale:
As a reviewer from exactly this pool, I would reject the pivot AS HEADLINED in one sentence: eps_cls + eps_pred cannot bound P(collision) because missed detections sit outside every conformal certificate in the chain (Timans calibrates on IoU-matched true positives), and FN rate rises with the very density shift the title advertises. The math lane confirms three more kills: per-(agent,timestep) unions yield ~4.6 m tubes and 67k–1.35M calibration trajectories (vacuous and infeasible); ACI inside the headline silently converts a hitting-event probability into a time-average that concentrates failures in dense moments; SDD-calibrated tubes deployed on a forward-facing D435i break exchangeability outright.

But the dossier also shows the honest version is both provable and genuinely open: a per-detected-track, per-episode bound at eps=0.1 (latched class-conditional eps_cls=0.02, per-agent time-shaped tubes with explicit H<=10 union at eps_pred=0.08, deterministic occlusion-shadow and body-floor branches). No 2023–2026 work composes classification-set-gated constraint hardness with prediction tubes into one P(collision-with-human) certificate for dynamic agents; the Sundarsingh RA-L 2026 paper is static and joint-not-class-conditional, Lindemann's 2602.12616 owns generic density shift but not Mondrian class-x-density, and the deterministic FN branch is MORE novel to this lineage, which assumes perfect perception. That is a strong RA-L paper — if every overclaim is surgically removed before drafting.

So the pivot direction is right, which eliminates C: a planner-only paper is incremental systems work to this audience, plays poorly with the exact target labs, and gifts the 6–9-month kernel window to the group most likely to close it. Between A and B, B dominates because the marginal cost of the planner letter is near zero (the system is built, 19/19 golden, demos exist — it is a write-up, sequenced Oct–Nov) while the marginal value is an insurance floor for December PhD applications on a zero-buffer build. A as specified is also over-scoped: both lanes independently conclude the second-planner plug-and-play demo is the only cuttable item that does not touch the theorem, and multi-planner evaluation alone is weak novelty reviewers will call "just evaluation." The binding engineering constraint is not conformal machinery at all — it is replacing constant-velocity prediction (0.9 m vs 2.0 m terminal tubes = passable vs blocked corridor) plus the FN branch and in-sim end-to-end calibration, which together fit ~60 working days only if the second planner and pre-September side-paper work are cut.
